newsitem.title: UK: UK's BOC to sell Ohmeda health care business.
newsitem.headline: UK's BOC to sell Ohmeda health care business.

text.p: British chemical group BOC said on Wednesday it was putting up for sale its Ohmeda health care business to allow BOC to concentrate on its other businesses.

BOC Group Chief Executive Danny Rosenkranz said Ohmeda's Ohmedas management team have "made significant improvements" over the past couple years but that it would have better development possibilities as part of a larger integrated health care business.
"It is in my view an attractive acquisition for a prospective purchaser, " Rosenkranz said.

Ohmeda's businesses comprise the development and manufacture of anaesthetics and critical care pharmaceuticals; anaesthesia delivery and patient monitoring systems; manufacture and development of disposable catheters and other vascular access and monitoring devices and the production and sale of infant care and suction and oxygen therapy products.
Ohmeda employs about 4,800 people in some 30 countries. In the year to September 30, 1996, its turnover was 506 million pounds ($849.5 million) and operating profit was 53 million pounds.
